edited_fraction: 3,846 to 2,152,928 modified weights per program (257 for SCAN, 21,482 for BabyAI)
cost_reported: sessions take 30-130 minutes; CIFAR-10, SCAN and BabyAI sessions cost US$5-13 at API prices (US$7.12-13.08 per ViT-Lite session); rerunning a kept program takes a few minutes with no LLM call
evidence_notes: WSP is the method: Claude Opus 5.5 works in a Python kernel and writes programs that compute weight edits from weights, activations and a few labelled checks (p.3, appendix), so code_or_tensor_tool and closed_loop. Largest target is ResNet-18 at 11.7M weights (p.3). Comparisons include eight fine-tuning methods, fixed references and a random-units control (Tab. 10). A post hoc non-LLM gated search reaches +24.12 against the program's +31.75 on ViT-Lite noise (p.~24). Success criteria and a counting rule were set by the authors, the rule after two sessions had been read (p.14), so prereg none. Code at github.com/Gen-Verse/WeightCode (p.1).
